chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah the Exalted has expanded in the sustenances of the foolish ones, so that the intellectuals may take lesson, and they may know that the world and whatever is in it is not attained by action nor by means.
ai.seo_question: Why does God give wealth to the foolish according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the disparity in sustenance, noting that Allah expands the provision of the 'foolish' (al-hamqa) to serve as a lesson for the 'wise' (al-uqala). This phenomenon underscores the Shia theological principle that worldly success is not strictly bound by human merit or strategy, but is ultimately a divine decree (qadr) intended to humble the intellect and remind believers that true benefit lies beyond mere material accumulation. The narration highlights the distinction between intellectual capability and divine favor, urging the wise to recognize the transient nature of dunya.
